The client-facing document is something you present to a potential client to introduce and explain your service.

For example, imagine a business owner encounters your service for the first time.

  1. On your website: They visit your Services page and read about your offering and the ten areas of marketing infrastructure you help businesses build.

I suggest we create them one at a time, in the right order, so that all three documents communicate the same service but serve different purposes.

We shouldn't simply take the ten pillars and copy them into three different documents. We need to decide what each document should communicate, how much detail it should contain, and what action we want the reader to take.

Here's how I would approach it.

Step 1. Establish your core service identity

Before designing any of the documents, we need to establish the central message that connects them.

This includes:

  • Service name: What do you call this overall service?

  • Service description: What exactly do you help businesses build?

  • Business problem: What problems does your service solve?

  • Value proposition: Why should a business invest in this instead of simply hiring someone to run ads or manage social media?

  • Target clients: What types and sizes of businesses are you serving?

  • Your approach: How do you assess, design, implement and improve their marketing infrastructure?

This becomes the foundation for all three documents.

Step 2. Create the three client-facing documents

Document 1: Service brochure

Create first

Purpose: Introduce and sell your service.

It should communicate:

  • Who you are and what you offer.

  • The problems businesses face.

  • Your solution and its benefits.

  • The ten service pillars, explained simply.

  • What clients can expect.

  • How to engage your services.

Format: A polished PDF, suitable for WhatsApp, email and website downloads.

Document 2: Service presentation

Purpose: Explain your service in greater depth during a meeting or consultation.

It should communicate:

  • Your philosophy and methodology.

  • How the ten pillars work together.

  • Your implementation process.

  • What you investigate and build.

  • The outcomes and value of the completed infrastructure.

Format: A professional PowerPoint or PDF slide deck.

Document 3: Client proposal

Purpose: Present a specific solution to an individual business.

It should communicate:

  • Your understanding of their business.

  • Their identified problems and gaps.

  • The pillars requiring attention.

  • Recommended activities and deliverables.

  • Project scope, timeline and responsibilities.

  • Fees, payment terms and next steps.

Format: A customizable proposal document, usually PDF.

Service brochure

Creates awareness and interest

Service presentation

Client proposal

Converts interest into a defined project

The website should actually be one of the most important places where your client-facing service information lives.

In fact, I would treat it as a fourth client-facing asset, not just another place to upload your brochure.

Unlike the brochure, which is a document you send to someone, your website is your permanent online business presence. It should explain your service, establish credibility, attract potential clients and generate enquiries.

How I would structure your website

I recommend a professional website with the following pages:

1. Home page

Introduce what you do, who you help, the problems you solve and why businesses need your service.

Include a clear call to action, such as Book a consultation.

2. About page

Explain your philosophy, approach, expertise, methodology and what makes your service different.

3. Services page

Introduce your overall service and explain the ten pillars in client-friendly language.

This is where visitors understand the breadth of what you offer.

4. Our approach / How it works

Explain your process: business assessment, strategy, infrastructure development, implementation, testing and optimization.

5. Case studies / Our work

Show actual projects, problems identified, solutions implemented and measurable outcomes.

If you are starting without case studies, this page can initially feature illustrative demonstrations clearly labelled as such.

6. Contact / Book a consultation

Provide an enquiry form, business contact details and a clear way to schedule an initial discussion.

7. Insights / Resources

Publish useful articles about marketing infrastructure, customer acquisition, conversion, analytics, automation and business growth.

This also supports your organic search and authority-building strategy.

How the website fits with the other client-facing materials

Asset

Its primary job

Website

Attract, educate, establish credibility and generate enquiries

Service brochure

Introduce your offering in a shareable format

Service presentation

Explain your methodology during meetings

Client proposal

Present a customized project and commercial offer

All four should communicate the same service positioning and use consistent branding.

One important distinction

Your website should not simply list ten pillars and stop there.

It should help a business owner recognize a problem they may not even know they have.

For example, a business might be spending money on advertising but:

  • Cannot identify which campaigns generate actual customers.

  • Has no proper lead management process.

  • Loses potential customers during checkout.

  • Does not follow up with previous customers.

  • Has disconnected marketing tools.

  • Cannot measure its true marketing performance.

Your website should demonstrate how your overall service addresses these interconnected problems.

The order I recommend

  1. Establish your service identity, name and positioning.

  2. Define the website structure and page content.

  3. Create the website.

  4. Develop the service brochure.

  5. Develop the presentation.

  6. Develop the proposal template.

The website and brochure should share the same foundational messaging, so we can develop their content together before designing either.

My recommendation is to treat the website as your main client-facing platform, with the other three materials supporting it throughout your sales process.
